If I had to sum this game up in two words, those two words would be frustratingly addictive. 

You will die. A lot. 

Don't make the assumption that this is a run-and-gun game. This is a thinking mans psychedelic 80's murder simulator. You will die learning a map layout. You will die figuring out when enemies will respond to gunfire. You will die due to glitchy doors. There is a lot of you dying in this game. But guess what there's also a lot of?

Heart-pumping Adrenaline-gorged violence. No other game evokes the same sense of crazed desperateness as you pummel some poor Russian mobsters face into the dance floor, only to get up a split second later, grab his shotgun, and blow away the other Russian Mobsters who've been unfortunate to be in the same building as you.

While the action is split second and fast-paced, the game rewards tactical planning and thinking more than twitch reactions. You will not succeed trying to run through a building swinging a baseball bat like a madman. You're going to have to bait enemies, burst into a room when no one's looking, and die several times perfecting ways to murder people.

My only complaint is how vague the boss fights are. While I've only encountered two thus far, both of them have been pretty vague on how you actually win them. How the hell was a I supposed to figure out that I could only damage biker once he's throw his weapon when [i]that isn't how the gameplay mechanics works at any other point previously?[/i]. The boss battles are inconsistent with the rest of the game.

It can get frustrating, but it is intensely satisfying when you've cleared four separate floors after countless deaths trying. [b]8/10, would recommend.[/b]

Hotline Miami is a game that truly carved out its own niche, a pulsating, neon-drenched fever dream that is as addictive as it is brutal.

The Good:
Visceral and Addictive Gameplay: At its core, Hotline Miami is about fast-paced, top-down action. Each level is a puzzle box of enemies and objectives. The gameplay loop of planning, executing, and often dying spectacularly, only to immediately restart, is incredibly addictive. The brutal efficiency of the combat, where a single mistake means instant death, forces players to be quick-thinking and precise.

Unique Aesthetic and Atmosphere: The game's 1980s Miami setting is brought to life with a stunning neon-noir aesthetic. The vibrant colors, the synthwave soundtrack, and the surreal, dreamlike narrative create an unforgettable atmosphere. The soundtrack, in particular, is a masterpiece, perfectly complementing the on-screen chaos and enhancing the game's overall mood.

Challenging but Fair: While notoriously difficult, Hotline Miami is generally fair. Deaths feel like a result of player error rather than cheap mechanics. Mastering the levels requires pattern recognition, quick reflexes, and a willingness to learn from mistakes. The variety of masks, each offering a unique gameplay advantage, adds another layer of strategic depth.

Compelling Narrative: Beneath the hyper-violence lies a dark and thought-provoking narrative. The story explores themes of addiction, violence, and the blurred lines between reality and delusion, leaving players with much to ponder long after the credits roll.

The Bad:
Repetitive Gameplay Loop: While addictive, the core gameplay loop can become repetitive for some players. The formula of entering a room, clearing it, and moving to the next can feel a bit samey over extended play sessions, especially if you get stuck on a particular level.

Steep Difficulty Curve: The game's high difficulty can be a significant barrier for some. While it's generally fair, the unforgiving nature and the need for split-second reactions might prove frustrating for players not accustomed to challenging action games.

Occasional Frustration: Despite its fairness, there will be moments of intense frustration. The sheer speed at which things can go wrong, combined with the instant restarts, can sometimes feel punishing, leading to moments where you might want to throw your controller.

Simple Level Design: While functional and serving the gameplay well, the actual level design itself can be somewhat simplistic in its layout. The focus is clearly on the action and puzzle-solving within those spaces, rather than architectural marvels.

Overall, Hotline Miami is a landmark indie title that delivers a potent cocktail of style, substance, and pure adrenaline. Its unique blend of challenging gameplay, unforgettable atmosphere, and a compelling narrative makes it a must-play for fans of action and stylish indie games, provided they can stomach the difficulty.

Before you buy this game, here's four questions to ponder.
Question 1: Do you like intense, action-packed, difficult, frustrating, yet satisfying gameplay?
Question 2: Do you like good music, generally in the vaporwave/retrowave genre?
Question 3: Do you like interesting stories, woven together in small pieces?
And the final question:
Do you like hurting other people?

Do you want to play a fast paced, top-down shooter with a great pixelated aesthetic, over the top gore, and an amazing soundtrack that will have you banging your head to the beat while shooting up bad guys? If that at all sounded appealing to you, get this game, because that is what this games sets out to do, and it achieves that perfectly. I know I used a bunch of words in that description (great, amazing, and perfect) that are all overused in reviews so much that they have all basically lost all meaning, but I couldn’t think of any other way to describe how impressed I am with with this game.
 
[h1] Pros: [/h1]

[b]Story[/b] I’m not going to say [strike]much[/strike] anything about it so I don’t spoil it, but I loved the story. A game like this doesn’t really even need a good story, just something to bring you from level to level, but this game went above and beyond.
 
[b]Feel[/b] I was going to put Art Style and Music in two separate categories, but couldn’t because of how well they complement each other to make both much better. The art style and music are the definition of “The whole is greater than the sum of its parts” They work so well together to create an amazing feel to the game that works so well with the gameplay and the story (which also work together to be greater than the sum of their parts)
 
[b]Core Gameplay[/b] Like the rest of this game, it’s amazing. The controls are tight, the game makes you feel powerful, the scoring system is done well, anything you can think of is just good.
 
[b]High Octane[/b] Do you like high octane games? Well good, because this is a high octane game. Now, I’m not entirely sure what “high octane” means, but I’ve heard a [i]lot[/i] of games described as high octane, and Hotline Miami is the embodiment of those games.
 
[b]Fun[/b] This game is really FUN. I had a blast playing it, and you probably will too
 
 
[h1] Cons: [/h1]
 
[b]Controls[/b] The controls took a little bit to get used to, specifically picking up and throwing weapons, but once I got used to it the problem was basically nonexistent. The only other problem I had with the controls was when selecting things in the menu, you use the arrow keys to change what you’re selecting, and then click with the mouse to choose it. It’s a bit weird and unintuitive, but it's not too bad because it doesn’t really affect the game, just the menu.
 
[b]Length[/b] It took me about 6 hours to play through the story, and the game is so great I wish it were much longer. Though, it does have masks and weapons to unlock, achievements to play for, and the levels are scored so it’s fun to try to beat your highscore, so it’s not too bad.
 
[h1] Conclusion [/h1] I originally meant for this review to be like 3 lines, but this game is so amazing, once I started writing and thinking about how good it is, I couldn’t stop writing. So yeah. Seriously, get this game.

I put off playing Hotline Miami for far too long. Despite knowing of its impact and legacy in the indie scene and being a fan of top-down action, I always passed up the game in my mind as being just a gore fest. While it's a very violent game, it also serves as a deconstruction of violence in video games as a whole, which ended up really earning my respect.

[i]Do you like hurting other people? Who are leaving messages on your answering machine? Where are you right now? And the final question: Why are we having this conversation?[/i]

These are questions posed early on in the game and it only outright gives one answer through dialogue by the end of the game. This leaves a lot of room for player interpretation, there's a real question of [i]why[/i] the player and the character are both so willing to commit so much violence for seemingly mundane reasons. It's fantastic storytelling done through gameplay as much as it's done through dialogue.

The gameplay itself does stand out as well, the graphics are constantly disorienting with wavy camera movement and neon colors leads to intense yet surreal action moments. You usually die in one shot and so do enemies, so every level has a puzzle element as it's never as simple as charging through the whole level, especially when different enemies must be killed in different ways.

Easily one of the highlights of the game was the decision to use many different artists being used for individual missions. It gives each level a unique feel while still being cohesive in identity, and is a great way to be exposed to new artists.

Hotline Miami is a very important piece of art that also survives the test of time, as its very blunt and bleak view on violence in the world only becomes more relevant as time goes on, this game and its sequel are must plays.

Hotline Miami was one of those games I picked without any information about it. Picked it up only because I'd heard the soundtrack and wanted to find out what the game was about. What I was not expecting was finding out it would be one of my favorite games ever.

At first, picking up the game, it's pace and understanding the controls can be somewhat confusing, but in the long run, you start to get the feel of it, start rushing into rooms and planning strategies of attack and, in a sort of way, you get into the character with one objective: kill, kill. Speaking of killing, the message of the game is clear. When I started to get more into the characters' minds, I understood what the developers wanted to transmit with this game. One message was repeated and resonated with me throughout the game: "Do you like hurting people?" That made me start to question the essence of the game, and its violence. For most of the game we don't really know why we're doing what we're doing. We just receive a phone call and we do it. And we kill without questioning. And the ecstasy of clearing a room is fun. In some ways, the creators of this game criticize its own violence. Why are we killing? Why do we continue to do it? Why does it feel good? Do I like hurting people?

The game also reflects on the United States ideology of its nationalism with more information hidden at the end of the game. I won't focus too much on this topic so as not to give too many spoilers, but the critic is pretty clear throughout the entire game.

Overall, Hotline Miami is a fantastic game that deserves to be in the hall of best indie games ever made. A highly recommended title as a game and a social critic.

Hotline Miami - A Brutal and Stylish Ballet of Violence

Rating: ★★★★★

Review:

Hotline Miami is a heart-pounding, adrenaline-fueled trip into the dark underbelly of the '80s. This top-down shooter from Dennaton Games delivers a relentless onslaught of fast-paced action, mind-bending puzzles, and a pumping synthwave soundtrack that will have you hooked from the very first beat.

Set in the neon-drenched streets of Miami, Hotline Miami places you in the role of a nameless hitman, compelled to carry out a series of brutal and bloody missions. The gameplay is intense and unforgiving, requiring split-second reflexes and a strategic mind to navigate through each level.

What sets Hotline Miami apart is its stylish and distinctive aesthetic. The pixelated art style is complemented by vibrant colors, giving the game a retro charm that harks back to the era it pays homage to. The level design is meticulously crafted, with a variety of rooms, hallways, and obstacles that demand tactical thinking and precise execution.

The combat in Hotline Miami is a beautifully choreographed dance of death. Armed with an array of weapons ranging from shotguns to melee implements, you'll mow down enemies with brutal efficiency. Each kill is satisfyingly visceral, accompanied by splatters of pixelated blood and the thumping soundtrack that sets the pulse racing.

However, Hotline Miami isn't just about mindless violence. The game's narrative takes unexpected twists and turns, delving into themes of identity, morality, and the blurred lines between hero and villain. The cryptic story will keep you questioning the events and characters, adding an intriguing layer to the blood-soaked gameplay.

The soundtrack of Hotline Miami is an absolute standout. The synthwave tunes perfectly capture the essence of the '80s, with their pulsating beats and infectious melodies driving the action forward. The music not only serves as a backdrop but also acts as a motivator, pushing you to push your limits and execute your kills with style.

It's worth noting that Hotline Miami can be incredibly challenging. Enemies are ruthless and can dispatch you with a single hit, forcing you to adopt a trial-and-error approach as you learn from each death. While this level of difficulty may frustrate some players, the sense of accomplishment when you finally overcome a particularly challenging level is incredibly rewarding.

In conclusion, Hotline Miami is a violent ballet of mayhem and style. With its unique aesthetic, relentless gameplay, and an unforgettable soundtrack, it's a must-play for fans of fast-paced action and atmospheric storytelling. Just be prepared for a challenge and to lose yourself in the neon-soaked brutality of Hotline Miami's twisted world.

Don't take it the wrong way, there is some fun to be had here. If you enjoy extremely fast-paced top-down violence with a degree of luck, then this might be your sort of thing. For most folks, this will likely end up being more of a headache to play.

While it visually nails a retro vibe, this can also be to its own detriment. For some players, you may experience motion sickness or headaches after small amounts of play. The text pops out, vibrates, and changes colors. The game world wobbles a bit and has a static/VHS filter over it. The extremely fast nature of the gameplay can become visually exhausting after a while. The music can become throbbing or annoying during certain sequences.


I wouldn't call this game difficult, but brutally random. The AI and hit detection specifically. The AI in this game seem to have some kind of random omniscience. You can attack an enemy head on, and sometimes they'll instantly kill you. At other times, they won't even react. This is compounded by the fact that there is no wind up or hit spark for any attacks made by enemies. They only need to touch you and you are dead. They also have super speed, meaning you'll have only fractions of a second to react most of the time. 

Gun-toting enemies are especially egregious of this behavior. Sometimes you can sneak up on an gun armed opponent and K.O. them easily. At other times, they'll sense you immediately, do a 180 degree snap turn(like an aimbot), and kill you from several yards away. They'll even snipe you from outside your view. It's almost bizarre, as sometimes the AI purposely plays "poorly", as if to be a good sport about it. Occasionally, I'd encounter enemies who couldn't shoot straight, or had trouble turning. At other times, they'd resort to the same "snap and kill" behavior.

The big keyword here is "Sometimes", because that's pretty much this game in a nutshell. Sometimes the AI is brutally efficient to the point they might as well be cheating. At other times they are so clueless they won't hear gunshots even when you fire right next to them. Sometimes doors will cover you, and other times enemies will see you through them and shoot you. Sometimes you can fire a full-auto weapon and no enemies will come running, and other times the entire level will be alerted. Sometimes your weapon will hit the enemy, sometimes it misses entirely.


Which leads to the next point, the hit detection is very spotty. The weapon mechanics in this game are fun, but they also seem to not connect half the time. Melee weapons seem to hit in a cone in front of them, but if you are too close to your opponent, you'll do no damage. However, they can still hit within a certain distance. If you end up walking on top of your enemy before swinging or shooting(say, in a furious brawl with multiple opponents), too bad. They'll instant kill you and you'll be forced to restart.

Hotline Miami is a top-down shooter, where the player controls a character known as Jacket. You receive random phone calls which send you to different places to well… murder everyone on your path! 

Let me start out by saying I played this game at launch, but never finished the last couple of chapters. So I played most of the game twice now.

Gameplay is straight forward. You get to a new building which has multiple floors. You kill everyone on a floor, and move on to the next. If you die, you restart the floor. There’s a variety of weapons, both melee and ranged, and everything is basically a 1 hit 1 kill, including you. This means you can either go the guns blazing route, meaning you have to be quick and make sure you hit everyone before they hit you. Or you can go the more careful way of taking out enemies 1 by 1. I myself tried to combine these depending on the floor layout and enemy paths. There’s also unlockable masks you can put on that give you various slight advantages like being able to take 1 bullet before dying, walking faster, or being able to kill enemies by slamming doors into them. Enemies walk certain paths, and as soon as they hear or see you, they just run towards your position trying to kill you. So in the end quite straight forward and challenging at times, but nothing special. Some chapters are cleared faster than others due to difficulty, but they’re all perfectly doable and for me never got to the point that I actually got annoyed because I would always get at least a bit further then last time.

The story is really vague and not explained well. I read that if you collect certain objects in the game the story is explained when you finish the game. Personally i did not do this, and if you don’t the story is never properly explained. Not that I cared, since the game's main charm is obviously the combat, music and colors.

Graphics are gorey pixel style with some flashy colors. Nothing special but it holds up after years and fits the overall theme really well. Guns and melee sound nice and satisfying and the levels are accompanied by different electronic beats, where some of them are amazing to listen to and pump your energy and others are average at best. 

Everything comes and fits together well though. The chapters where the music is spot on really make the whole game feel different. Driven by the music and focus of making sure you’re not spotted you’re basically a murdering machine moving from room to room. This combined with the gorey pixelated graphics and flashy neon colors makes it a blast to play. 

Overall I recommend Hotline Miami to basically everyone to at least try. Especially in sales the game get’s dirt cheap and you should just give it a try. It’s on the shorter side but that’s okay if you ask me. It’s finishable in a couple of hours and you can add some more hours to this if you want to unlock all masks, want to improve your combo scores etc.

When you play until 3:30 in the morning to get an A+ score on a level, then you know the game has you by the balls :)

This game is set in the 80s in Miami, and that is for me already a reason not to miss out on this one. Hotline Miami is a top-down pixelated game, containing a lot of gore and violence. The game is mysterious and has trippy flashing colors, neon lights, VHS rental stores, blinking lights, shaking cameras and text. There is a large selection of (melee) weapons which you can use to kill/slaughter your enemies. While swinging your golf stick, bat, knife, dart or katana, you make your ways through 20 levels. I loved it where half dead people were crawling over the floor, super funny! (I am not sure how this sounds to the reader.)
 
Make sure you empty your uzi, shotguns and machineguns on hundreds of enemies, who always react faster than light and with an accuracy of a sniper. Take note that every touch/bullet of an enemy means instant death. I was a bit wondered that one of the first achievements I got was 'Die 1000 times', since in most game I try not to die at all or as less as possible. In this game dying is part of the game. The game is extremely fast paced and will bolster your reactions. The pumped up music fits very well to this game and is a joy to listen to.

To master the game and to get all achievements will take serious effort. To get A+ grades on all levels is mostly very doable except for the level 'Hot and Heavy'. To get A+ there, I wanted a 20x combo so bad that at a certain moment I think I started to look like the characters in this game. I am proud to have the "achievement whore" in this game :D. Your second-last achievement will be: Get A Life. Now as an achievement whore I have my life back and can sleep before 3:30 at night again, thank you for that!    

If you like games that brutally punish you for the slightest mistake, play this game. The way points explode after every kill, or the fact that the music never stops when you die, leaves you no other option than to continue the game until you end up as an achievement whore like me.

An indie so foundational that it feels generic, with a meta-narrative so overdone in the years since that it feels cliche. Hotline Miami is, of course, neither generic nor cliche. It is a game that redefined notions of what a small team can unleash upon this industry, and that brought extreme violence back into the center of our interest. Joseph Liberman rejoice, the murder simulator never died.

Along with the astounding gameplay, its crooked nature of the story, chaperoned by the swirling psychedelic soundscapes will most likely draw other people in & captivate them.

Hot damn this just has a retro arcade visual style mixed with easy to pick up hard to master mechanics, its addictive, fast paced, and delightfully frantic. Even though you die in one hit (unless you take someone hostage), the quick respawn system keeps the experience from ever feeling frustrating. The story is surprisingly strong as well, exploring our relationship with violence a thought provoking and even forward thinking concept for its time. The visuals have also aged incredibly well. Despite being released back in 2012, the game’s pixel art style remains timeless, looking just as sharp and stylish today as it did over a decade ago. That said, the game isn’t perfect. Every moment that isn’t focused on the core, second to second gameplay tends to drag. The boss fights, for example, feel more like glorified puzzles than actual encounters. They lack the intensity and decision making of the main gameplay loop, and once you’ve figured out their patterns, they become little more than roadblocks. It’s a shame, considering how excellent the core mechanics are. Level design can also be hit or miss, especially toward the later stages. Some maps are overly large, leading to cheap deaths from enemies you couldn’t even see. Combine that with the repeated dialogue sequences you’re forced to rewatch every time you restart, and it can make the frequent deaths more tedious than they need to be. Still, despite its flaws, this game remains a truly unique experience that I wholeheartedly recommend. Its highs easily outweigh its lows, and there’s really nothing else quite like it. Even its sequel couldn’t capture the same lightning in a bottle that this one did.

Some of them can be really helpful and remind me of games I wanted to play and never had a chance, or simply forgot, because of my unorganized past. Right now, I have another problem, even having my own library, it's so huge already, that I need a lot of time to categorize every game. So, that's how talking to other players really help.

That was a little interlude about how I was reminded about Hotline Miami. I was speaking to a guy, who have hundreds of hours on this game and also creating levels for its sequel. We never spoke about the game itself, but I really felt like a dumb, calling myself a gamer and never finishing Hotline Miami - amazing, brilliant, unique game, that blew millions of gamers minds in 2012. 

Hotline Miami is a masterpiece. I am not afraid to call it this way, because I know it for sure. What do you call a masterpiece? A well-made product, which combines amazing interesting gameplay, unique and inexpressible atmosphere, astonishing WOW-effect driving soundtrack, colourful characters with its own story and charisma, intriguing plot with twists and cliffhangers, mind-blowing graphics, special visual style and possibility to replay. So,HM has everything listed above, maybe except mind blowing graphics, but to be honest, this is not that type of game, where you want to care about this. 

Sets in alternative 1989 Miami, this game provides you an interesting thrilling story, about a mysterious guy, who keeps on getting messages with new contracts on his answering machine. First levels you will be getting in a mood of the game, trying to understand the whole mechanics and how everything works in there. The moment you will already fall in love with game, you will begin to understand, that the whole game and story is not only about a random person, killing others for money as a mercenary, it’s something bigger. But, no spoilers ahead, you gotta see and feel everything by yourself. 

For a new players, game can seem ridiculously difficult, but it’s only for the first few levels and the moment you’ll understand how it works you will be enjoying it for a long long time. This game can be challenging at some levels and you can be mad af on yourself, especially when you are trying to finish the level with an impossible scenario and outnumbered enemies for 30 minutes and then you are distracted by the phone call and the last guy on the floor kills you. And one quick tip - you will start to hate doors after this game so much! The whole door mechanics in the game is just insane and can make you lose your mind. But, when you’ll realize how it works, you’ll start to use it in a tactical way, that can lead you to the win easily.

So, to make a long story short and to sum everything up!

What can you say about Hotline Miami that hasn't already been said? It made waves when it came out in 2012, equally horrifying players with its brutal violence and delighting them with its bubbly synthwave soundtrack. It's a game of contradictions, confusion, and finding truth amid a number of neon-soaked bloodbaths. I loved every minute of it.

Hotline Miami places you in 1989 Florida, where a man in a varsity jacket is threatened into committing spree killings by mysterious messages left on his answering machine. To hide his identity, he uses masks that seemingly grant him special powers - for example, "Don Juan" turns any door into a killing machine, "Peter" silences all of the player's gunshots, and "Rasmus" makes it easier to identify objects scattered around levels. The narrative here is mostly nameless, as only a handful of characters get proper introductions. This gives the story a very odd, abstract feeling to it. Just who are these people that our protagonist is meeting? Does his friend at the grocery store know more about the killings than he's letting on? Are the masked men who visit him nightmares or something more real? Though the game does provide some answers, the player is forced to draw their own conclusions on several plot points.

The gameplay is similar to other top-down twin-stick shooters, but with one major difference: you and most enemies die in one hit. Fortunately, restarts are instant and are relegated to your current floor. This gives you plenty of room for experimentation. Are enemies too scattered to make ambushes work? Grab an assault rifle and gun them down from a distance. Need a weapon at the level's opening? Put on the Dennis mask and carve up those immediate enemies with a knife. Your only objective is to kill everyone in a targeted building, and the game gives you numerous ways to do so. You can bash them with melee weapons, shoot them with shotguns or SMGs, or knock them to the floor and beat their heads in. Eurogamer called the game a "top down fuck em up," and I can safely say that is an appropriate title to give it.

Hotline Miami's soundtrack is a bouncy throwback to the synth songs of 80s action movies. Artists like MlOlOlN, Jasper Byrne, and Perturbator get their chances to shine in the disturbingly-fitting combat. You may not associate electronic music with mass murder before Hotline Miami, but you definitely will once you finish the game. The entire soundtrack is fantastic (and worth buying along with the game!), but some more variety might have been nice. The first half of the game has the tendency to use the same song at least twice in levels. It isn't a serious issue, but it feels like a missed opportunity to bring more talent on board.

The replayability is strong. You can compete against yourself or others with the game's scoring system. Rack up higher combos or find ways to score more points, and you just might get an A+ on the level. There are also bonus masks, unlockable weapons, and puzzle pieces that can all be collected if you're a completionist. It can be somewhat difficult to find these items in the 2D landscape, but it isn't impossible to get them all without a guide.

Honestly, Hotline Miami may be one of my favorite games of all time. Minor complaints aside, I can't find much fault with it. It is difficult, but it feels fair in the way its challenges work. Its length is enough without wearing out its welcome. The gameplay is varied, and almost any level can be completed in dozens of different ways. Dennaton Games knocked it out of the park on all fronts. I would highly recommend buying it at full price. It's worth every penny.

Hotline Miami is a top-down brutally gory pixel shooter that's action packed, challenging and lots of fun. This game is one of my all time favorite indie games and it will stay that way for a long time. The mechanics for the game are interesting, the  dark story is hard to follow the first time playing through the game but later you'll really enjoy it. The sort of 80s retro soundtrack is really really fun, it gives the game feel a lot more of an atmospheric feel.

Personally after beating the game 3 times, every once in a while I just jump in and have a bit of fun finishing some of my old favorite levels. The combat feels smooth, there is a wide variety of guns, melee and throwable weapons. Mechanics in the game are very awesome, you have different masks that each have their own powers, some are more useful than others and some just add extra challenge to experienced players. There are really only a few bad things I can say about this game, and those are listed below.

[b] Positives: [/b]
+Super fun.
+Fast paced combat.
+Crazy gunplay.
+Bloody and gory.
+Lots of weapons.
+Different masks each with their own skills.
+Amazing pixel art graphics.
+Good story.
+Great sound effects and really nice retro soundtrack.
+Each level has it's own sort of way, none of the levels are linear but there is always one objective, kill everyone.
+Satisfying kills.
+For some people (like me) replayability is very good.

[b] Negatives: [/b]
-Game is pretty short, you can beat the game in around 5 hours.
-Some major bugs which people use as exploits in levels, allowing you to beat the levels with ease.
-Only 2 boss fights in the game, both quiet boring and easy, each take around 3 mins to beat.
-Some really overpowered masks.
-As much as the story is good, it's quiet linear, no backstory or anything on any of the character, we barley get any names.

[b] Both: [/b]
-&+ AI is usually alright, but can sometimes be really broken and stupid.
-&+[spoiler] Some levels use a different character that has different mechanics, some people like him but I don't really like him. [/spoiler]
-&+ Some masks that are funny, but are annoying to get and don't serve any really purpose other than a small joke. [spoiler] The fish mask that is a reference to Phil Fish, the maker of FEZ for example, all it does is turn all the text in the game into horribly butchered French. [/spoiler]

Overall I rate this game an [b] 8.5/10 [/b] it does have it's flaws but it's still 100% worth picking up if you want a nice addition to your library and enjoy a challenge.

Hotline Miami is a shining example how a retro game should be. You are Jacket, an ingame unnamed person who gets wierd calls which lead him to the russian mafia during the 80s in miami. Your objective is to kill everyone of them in the most brutal and spectacle way possible without getting a bullet in the face. 

The Story is not the focus of the game, but is still told very competently. The main meat of this game lies in its gameplay. Your enemys die in one hit, as do you (unless your very lucky). You can pick up weapons from the floor, both melee and firearms and begin to violently kill every mobster. The better the time, the more kills in succession and the most creative kills earn you better scores which adds a nice reason for multiple replays, as do the masks you find during the game. The masks give you different abilities, such as killing enemys with only your fists, running faster, killing enemys with thrown weapons and much more. In case of your death (and believe me you will die) you have to press just a single button and can get right back into the action at the last checkpoint without any load times. Thanks to all that you get a very frantic but extremly addictive game, that is both challenging as well as rewarding.

The combat itself is what makes the game feel really good though. Hitting an enemy with a door in the face, slamming a baseball bat right through his skull or shooting his vital organs onto the floor, everything has a nice impact feeling.

The music in this game is amazing and i cant praise it enough. Multiple artists created a beautiful recreation of old 80s electronic music.

Hotline Miami is a tight, compact experience that tempers its immaculate presentation and buckets of bloody fun with moments of thoughtful introspection.

Gameplay is simple and intuitive, getting a lot of mileage out of a scant few buttons, and the levels function as puzzles with multiple solutions depending on playstyle and player expression. Frustration does rear its head at certain points. The boss battles are unexciting and painfully linear, and it can be incredibly exasperating when the limited control scheme works against you or your perfect combo is cut short by getting shotgun sniped across the map through six layers of glass by the one goon you forgot to bash. Other than these momentary dips, the levels are consistent in quality across the board, and the scoring system gives perfectionists and masochists plenty of opportunities to hone their craft.

Gameplay aside, I think where Hotline Miami really shines is the subtle narrative framing that examines player agency and our relationship to violence in this medium. The opening tutorial wastes no time in inciting the bloodshed with "I'm here to tell you how to kill people." Once the killing starts, it doesn't stop, but your motivations, your purpose, and your enjoyment of it are constantly questioned within the text of the story and the moments of Sisyphean quiet between levels.

If you want it to be, Hotline Miami can easily be enjoyed as a fun shoot 'em up on its own merit. But underneath the dripping red pixels and the pulsing synthwave beats, Hotline Miami holds up a mirror that asks "Do you like hurting other people?"

Hotline Miami is a fun game, even 13 years after it first released in 2012.

Hotline Miami, one of Devolver Digital's most beloved titles that they have published over the years, is an indie that has earned its reputation as a violent and most intense top-down action game that is set in 80s Miami where you take control of a psychopath with a particular affinity for animal masks who is guided by various mysterious calls to clear out the shady and decrepit buildings that are home to many thugs and gangsters who are just as eager and quick to kill you in quite a brutal fashion!

Such is to expected from a game that, in some respects, is satirizing parts of what made Miami in the 80s so iconic (for better and for worse!) as I dare say that one of the finer aspects of this indie is by far the sharp yet almost 'psychedelic' artstyle that fits the chaotic mood of Hotline Miami whilst also hinting at the deranged state of 'Jacket' himself. This fond name given by the fans was not officially coined until the sequel, however it would seem that the developers behind Dennaton Games agreed with the community sentiment and gave the iconic masked protagonist the memorable name for sequels and cameos alike!

As for the tight gameplay itself here, Hotline Miami takes the approach of dealing with threats as efficiently and as fast as possible since you have an arsenal of melee weapons and firearms alongside the odd throwable object to utilize when dealing with various gangsters on each level. Typically these will have to be acquired on-site as each style has its own perks, melee weapons generally being ideal for silent killings to prevent the whole floor from quickly descending upon you, guns allowing for quick dispatching at a more safer range whilst throwable weapons offer silent kills at a distance higher than a blade or bat can reach but not to the degree of guns though can ricochet off walls in a way that bullets simply can not.

To further vary the gameplay up, the start of each level also prepares the protagonist with a choice of masks to choose from. These often provide a bonus to the player that will aid them in their psychotic killing spree, whether this be having a starting weapon already at hand or the ability to move faster, take more bullets from enemy gunfire or even preventing a certain canine enemy from attacking you. Other masks either provide a quirky 'neutral' element to gameplay or actually can make a level much harder by darkening vision or reversing controls!

Although the enemy variety isn't as beefy as other games out there, Hotline Miami opts to keep things simple by having three main types of enemies as typically an overwhelming majority will consist of the standard white suit thugs that come equipped with either a melee weapon or a gun to kill the player with. Following this are the canine Dobermanns I spoke of earlier that lack in health but more than make up for it in speed alongside the inability to be harmed by unarmed attacks. Finally there are the bulky black gangsters that are unarmed themselves but can easily make short work of Jacket with just their muscle alone, being immune to any melee attack alongside unarmed fists that makes guns essential to take down these foes that are more likely to survive bullets than the other enemies. There also exists one special type of enemy on a specific level pertaining to law enforcement that are actually immune to being killed but are prone to temporarily being stunned by melee weapons, a rare one-off that changes how you would typically finish a level once cleared of enemies.

Part of what I feel gives Hotline Miami such a memorable experience isn't just tied to its snazzy visuals that some have credited this very game as bringing about a resurgence in the 'synthwave' aesthetic + electronic music but with how it is very much a challenging game to overcome at first. Naturally newer and more cautious players will treat this as a tactical game that tests your fast reflexes, making you plan ahead for every step and what outcomes could potentially occur as each enemy has a set routine or position that they patrol on each floor. This can vary in not just the guns and melee weapons they wield but also how 'alert' some are since there is a noticeable difference in how perceptive enemies can be when you appear in their eyesight but also whenever a gun is fired as not all enemies will follow to investigate at first.

This 'RNG' element of the game, when combined with just how quickly the brutal action follows on both sides seeing how any successful attack from an enemy will kill Jacket just as he can easily dispose of enemies too with the right skillful approach to groups of gangsters, lends itself well to what I would refer to as a 'speed game' or, in other words, a speedrunner's wet dream. Seeing as the tight action gameplay evolves into a whole new level once you truly adopt the game's idea of being fully 'reckless' but backing it up with experience and confidence in the controls as a whole, plus with there being a surprising amount of tactics one can use to quickly dispose of enemies once you know how to take calculated risks and act on them quickly! (It helps as well that checkpoints are frequent with each floor saving progress mid-level so that the longer stages don't become too frustrating)

No doubt that this is quite an easy game to recommend for anyone who loves classic indie action at its finest, though it won't be for everyone either as I did note how it felt unusually short compared to my first time playing it on the PlayStation 4 port way back in 2015. However, I do feel that my personal nitpick over the game's length may very well be opposed by those who struggle to even get through the base game itself as Hotline Miami demands quick reactions from the player whilst maintaining a degree of precision when striking and aiming at the many gangsters you'll be asked to take down in bloody gore fashion.

All in all, I feel pretty confident about giving this a solid recommendation for anyone who has yet to experience this indie gem of a game that's seeking a nice thrill in retro style that is also not keen to shy away from some of the darker themes that Hotline Miami touches upon but, as I said before, this is one game that feels good to beat and arguably even better to dominate in which, depending on your skill level, may be a rare case of being an indie worth chasing to 100% completion!

TLDR Version:

• Well-designed action combat game from an eagle-eye perspective with a strong flavour of brutality and gore (+)
• Offers a good challenge for most average gamers but also serves as a great game to excel in and speedrun once the controls and mechanics are mastered (+)
• Hotline Miami provides a short yet captivating story that looks into the dark world of 80s Miami and all of the vices it holds, with an equally intriguing subtle background for those looking for it (+)
• Game difficulty is balanced well throughout the levels, providing multiple solutions to difficult problems in almost all levels of the game (+)
• The excellent blending of drug-fueled visuals combined with strong inspiration from the retrowave aesthetics to highlight the madness of Miami's senseless violence helps to make it quite the memorable experience

• Though Hotline Miami is beloved for its intense action, some may find the fast reflexes and quick thinking required in later levels to be too much to handle (-)
• The length of the game is a little on the short side, only providing 16 base game chapters and 4 post-game chapters alongside 2 additional bonus levels (-)
• Hotline Miami's psychedelic artstyle alongside the pixelated visuals could be off-putting to those looking for less visually-distracting indies (-)
